title: FuRA: Full-Rank Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Spectral Preconditioning
claim: Our method beats the full-capacity baseline on accuracy while matching the cheap method's speed and using the least memory.
layout: 1 panel, three grouped horizontal bar clusters, legend on top, bold best values
description: A single horizontal grouped bar chart with a legend across the top: blue for FuRA (ours), gray for LoRA, red-orange for Full FT. There are three metric groups, stacked vertically and labeled on the left. Score (Avg., higher is better) shows FuRA at 88.01, LoRA at 83.46 and Full FT at 86.64. Time (s/step, lower is better) shows FuRA at 0.046, LoRA at 0.043 and Full FT at 0.201. Memory (GB, lower is better) shows FuRA at 22.7, LoRA at 26.8 and Full FT 76.9. Numeric values sit at the bar ends, and the best value in each group is bold. The eye goes first to the long blue score bar, then to the long red bars for time and memory.
caption: \method\ delivers higher accuracy than Full FT with LoRA-level runtime and the lowest GPU memory.
abstract: Both full fine-tuning (Full FT) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods such as LoRA introduce weight updates without accounting for the spectral structure established during pretraining. As a result, noisy gradients from limited fine-tuning data can perturb robust pretrained features. We identify spectral preconditioning as the missing ingredient: reparameterizing each weight matrix through its full-rank singular value decomposition (SVD) and freezing one singular basis constrains updates to the pretrained column space, yielding a preconditioned optimization scheme that outperforms unconstrained Full FT at the same trainable parameter count. Building on this insight, we propose FuRA (Full-Rank Adaptation), an efficient full-rank adaptation framework based on a block tensor-train factorization W = LSR, where the large core L is fixed to the pretrained block-wise SVD basis, while only the compact core R and the block-wise singular values S are optimized. This design simultaneously provides full-rank spectral preconditioning, preserves full-rank update expressivity, and achieves parameter, memory, and step-time efficiency comparable to LoRA. FuRA consistently outperforms Full FT across multiple settings, including LLM fine-tuning (+1.37 on LLaMA-3-8B commonsense reasoning), LLM reinforcement learning for mathematical reasoning, and visual instruction tuning for VLMs. Furthermore, the 4-bit quantized variant, QFuRA, also surpasses QLoRA. Code is available at https://github.com/yequanzhao/FuRA
